title: An Empirical Design Justice Approach to Identifying Ethical Considerations in the Intersection of Large Language Models and Social Robotics

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative thematic analysis of participant interactions with the robot using non-English languages and code-switching, assessing language capability asymmetries and the exclusionary impacts on indigenous languages.

Thematic analysis of participant reflections during the co-design of the robot's physical and non-physical traits, exploring concerns about the reinforcement of feminine stereotypes, docileness, and gender binarization in social AI.

Thematic analysis of participant feedback during the co-design workshops, focusing on the lack of ethnic diversity in the robot's appearance options and the risk of reinforcing harmful racialized logics.

Qualitative analysis of neurodivergent participants' interactions with the robot, evaluating how pre-programmed non-verbal cues (such as constant eye contact) can cause discomfort and fail to accommodate diverse social and communicative norms.

Thematic analysis of open-domain dialogues on sensitive topics (e.g., queer identity, feminism, anarchism), critiquing the robot's pre-programmed guardrails and its adherence to a specific, non-neutral set of Western politically correct values.
